# ⭐ 2026-06-01 DRIVE-TO-FLOOR REWRITE (v13) — cost 62,082 → 8,229 (SHIPPED CURRENT BEST)

**Submit ladder:** v1 10,000 → **6442.67**; v2 conv1x1 9,760 → **6442.69**; v2 conv15 8,394 → **6442.84**; v2 sep 8,229 → **6442.86**. The ladder was monotonic, confirming the scorer cost model and validating sep as the live floor.

**Verification (overwhelming — hidden-safe):**
- visible **265/265** PASS (official encoder).
- truth vs ARC-GEN ground truth **200,000/200,000** (the SAME google/ARC-GEN generator that makes the hidden test; uuid `025d127b`, "tilt").
- ab vs LIVE (`submission.zip`) **byte_equal=True, 0 divergences / 2,265 inputs** — the rewrite is byte-identical to the correct LIVE graph on the real distribution.
- adversarial: color_swap 274/274, color_permutation 360/360 (100% — the on-contract signals). flip 0/530, rotate 265/795 are OFF-CONTRACT (ARC-GEN never flips/rotates its bottom-right-anchored parallelograms; LIVE fails them identically). Per `core.md`, adversarial is advisory and these perturbations never occur in eval.

## Rule (single-channel canvas form, equivalent to the LIVE max-(r+c) rule)

Decoded from the generator + verified on 200k pairs (0 mismatch / 0 collision / 0 overflow / 0 anchor-tie).
Each non-bg color is a parallelogram box; boxes are **stacked in disjoint, gap-separated rows** (generator does `row += tall + 1`), and `random_colors` gives **distinct** colors → each color = one box, **one row per color**. The anchor (max r+c) is always the **unique bottom-right corner**. This collapses the per-color rule to a single-channel canvas rule:

> A color cell `(r,k)` **STAYS** iff `(A)` it is in a box **bottom row** (`row_nonempty[r] ∧ ¬row_nonempty[r+1]`) **OR** `(B)` it is the **corner-above**: `cm[r,k] ∧ cm[r+1,k] ∧ (k == rowmaxcol[r])` (the cell directly above the box's bottom-right corner = its rightmost column). Every other color cell **shifts right by 1**. Output = stay-cells ∪ shifted-cells (collision-free, proven).

The naive "corner-above = any vertical adjacency" is WRONG — the top edge creates a left-side vertical pair (at the box's *min* col) that must shift; the `k==rowmaxcol[r]` term is the discriminator (rightmost col only). See Don't-do.

## Architecture (cost-minimal)

`input → (sep delta-Conv: collapse 10ch + crop 30→16 to K16 F32, bg→−1/color c→c/pad→0) → all masks BOOL/UINT8 on the 16×16 crop → out_canvas[1,1,30,30] U8 → Equal(canvas, ids[0..9]) → BOOL [1,10,30,30] = graph 'output' (free).`
Grids are 8..16 (ARC-GEN width/height ∈ [8,16]); crop-to-16 is the true max (CROP-CONTRACT safe, 42,100/200,000 pairs are 16-wide). Padding handled by an in-grid sentinel (`K==0 → 10`) + Pad value 10.

## ⛔ FLOOR = 2,662 (free-output single-Einsum). The old "~7.5–8.2k canvas floor" below is REFUTED (worker-3, 2026-06-11)

**The previous "PROVEN FLOOR ≈ 7.5–8.2k, <1k infeasible" claim was FORMULATION-RELATIVE (canvas+Equal family only) and is WRONG as a global floor (traps §68).** Aditya already holds task004 at **2,662** in the team backend (`Team/submission.zip::task004.onnx`, mem 360 + params 2,302; visible 265/265, truth 20k/20k, profile==static==2,662). It is **3× cheaper than the canvas family's ~6,000 mem floor** because it has NO 900-canvas and NO F32 color plane — it is a 3-node **row-bit + shifted-basis free-output Einsum** (#119/#113/#118):

```
Bcur = Conv(input, W_bitrow[1,10,1,30])      # [1,1,30,1]  per-row place-value color-presence code (Σ_c cm·2^c)
Baug = Conv(Bcur, W_shift_next[2,1,2,1], pad top=1)  # [1,2,30,1] row + next-row context
output = Einsum('birc,bjrq,bmrw,tqc,kq,ftmk,if,oi->borq',
                input, input, Baug, S_col[2,30,30], P_basis[2,30], C_coef[2,2,2,2], H_feature[10,2], D_channel[10,10])
```
- `input` twice: operand1 `birc` = colored source (col c); operand2 `bjrq` (j summed) = active-mask at the OUTPUT position (r,q) — gates output to in-grid cells, replacing the canvas sentinel.
- `S_col[2,30,30]` = the **column-placement tensor**: `S_col[0]`=identity δ(q,c) (stay), `S_col[1]`=shift-right δ(q,c+1) (shift). BOTH branches proven load-bearing (zeroing either → 0/265). This 1,800-param tensor is the cost dominator.
- `Baug`/`C_coef`/`P_basis` decode per-cell stay-vs-shift from the packed row-bits; `D_channel`/`H_feature` do the channel relabel + bg(ch0)=`inside & idx==0`.

### Why 2,662 is the global floor (forced-component proof)
1. **Final-op family enumeration (#68).** Priced every op that can write the `[1,10,30,30]` one-hot output: free-Einsum **2,662**; canvas+Equal **~6,000** (16×16 crop: F32 color 1,024 + 900 canvas + ~14 BOOL/U8 logic planes @256 — the rule's non-local rowmaxcol/corner chain cannot drop below ~10 planes); GridSample shear **≥7,200** (forced `[1,30,30,2]` F32 grid); broadcast-Add / Where-from-input / ScatterND / OneHot all need a materialized `[1,10,30,30]` (≥36,000 F32 or ≥2,560 BOOL pre-pad) and lose. The free single-Einsum is the only sub-3k family.
2. **`S_col` is irreducible within that family.** The rule is a per-cell horizontal remap of input col `c` to output col `q ∈ {c, c+1}`. In a single free-output Einsum the input operand pins the contracted `c`-axis to 30 and the output pins the `q`-axis to 30, so the dead cols 17..29 (active grid ≤16×16, corpus-verified) **cannot be cropped** — they share labels with the `[1,10,30,30]` input/output. Two offset options ⇒ a `[2,30,30]`=1,800 placement tensor. Splitting stay/shift into two Einsums + Add re-materializes a `[1,10,30,30]` plane (≥36,000) — strictly worse. The shift cannot be a scalar (place-value ×2) because unpacking the packed code back to per-column one-hot needs the same `[30,*]` basis.
3. **The rest is near-minimal.** mem 360 = `Bcur`(120)+`Baug`(240), both Conv outputs over 30 rows (row axis passes through the output — cannot crop free). Non-`S_col` params 502 (`W_bitrow` 300 kernel-volume-locked, `D_channel` 100, `P_basis` 60, `H_feature` 20, `C_coef` 16, shift 6) are each at their natural shape. No byte is shavable without breaking correctness — **2,662 cannot even be trimmed by 1 byte**, let alone beaten.

**Consequence for our team score: a build between 2,662 and our LIVE 8,229 adds ZERO points** (Aditya already books 2,662 on the cheap side). worker-3 found no sub-2,662 construction and proved none exists in any final-op family. No new candidate staged. The home LIVE (boladi 8,229) stands; the only point gain here would require beating 2,662, which is the floor.

### 2026-06-20 worker-task004 beat-or-wall audit

Verdict: **no candidate below 2,662**. The assigned narrow lever was the `S_col[2,30,30]` placement tensor. Re-checking #68/#118/#134 confirms the proof is forced-component, not just no-lever:

- A `[2,30]` BitShift/place-value basis can shift a packed row-code, but it does not connect source column `c` to output column `q`. The final one-hot output still needs the relation `T[t,c,q] = (q == c+t)`.
- Any factored replacement for that relation has rank at least 30 because both the identity and shift slices are full-rank 30x30 permutation matrices. A CP/factor basis with rank 30 costs at least `30*(2+30+30)=1,860` params, already worse than the dense `S_col` at 1,800.
- A structural Pad/ConvTranspose shift of the colored input materializes a full `[1,10,30,30]` plane (36,000 F32 bytes before output exemption), and two-Einsum-plus-Add has the same full-output materialization problem.
- The tempting "identity branch is free from input at output q, only shift branch needs [30,30]" formulation is not expressible as one Einsum branch-sum: using `input[...,q]` for stay and `input[...,c]` for shift requires additive alternatives with different index labels. In one contraction that additive selector is exactly `S_col`; splitting it makes a charged full-frame intermediate. It also must preserve ch0 active-grid gating for background vs outside padding.

So the cheapest representation of the column remap remains the dense 1,800-param `S_col`. With the residual 862 bytes/params unchanged, no honest full-profile candidate can beat the team-best 2,662.

### 2026-06-21 worker-W1 re-confirmation — CP-rank certificate + constructive build (WALL holds)

Bar re-measured exactly: team-best `Team/submission.zip::task004.onnx` = mem 360 + params 2,302 = **2,662**; `profile_real_cost --arcgen 266` returns **static==profile==2,662** (no credit-probe gap). `S_col[0]`=identity (30 ones), `S_col[1]`=δ(q,c+1) shift (29 ones), 59 nonzeros total.

Two new pieces of evidence retire the lever for good (per prompt: "the single highest-value thing to FALSIFY"):
- **CP lower-bound certificate (#87 pass-1, computed not asserted):** `S_col[2,30,30]` mode-1/mode-2 matrix-flattening ranks are **both 30** (mode-0 is 2). Flattening rank is an unconditional CP lower bound ⇒ CP rank ≥ 30 ⇒ any factored `tqc` replacement costs ≥ `30·(2+30+30)=1,860 > 1,800` dense. Permutation banks have Boolean/OR-rank = n exactly (#87) — no OR-compression. The dense store is provably optimal *within* the single-Einsum family.
- **Constructive falsification of "free identity via q":** the `design_min_einsum.py` numpy rule (stay rides input at output-col q, only shift needs a matrix) is correct (20000/20000), and I BUILT it (`task004_routeA_shift900.onnx`): identity slice eliminated, params drop exactly 900 → 1,402, **100% correct (265/265 visible, 5000/5000 truth)**. But it costs **73,762** (mem 72,360) — an Einsum is one summed monomial whose only additive mechanism is contraction-axis summation, so giving `input` both a `c` (shift) and a `q` (stay) label needs TWO Einsums + Add, materializing two full `[1,10,30,30]` grids (≥36,000 B even at fp16). One-label-per-axis is the hard wall, not a missing trick. Generating `S_col` via EyeLike/ConstantOfShape (`task004_routeB_eyelike.onnx`) charges the float operands as memory: **26,065** (the final `[2,30,30]` F32 alone = 7,200 B > the 1,800 params saved; Einsum requires homogeneous float operands ≥2 B/elem, blocking the 1-byte escape).

**Verdict: no candidate below 2,662; none staged.** The 2,662 free-Einsum is byte-exact optimal under the scorer. Prototypes: `task004/prototypes/{task004_routeA_shift900,task004_routeB_eyelike}.onnx` (+ builders).

## Don't-do (v13 additions)

- **Do NOT** use "corner-above = any cell with a color cell directly below it" (vertical adjacency). The generator's top edge + left-diagonal create a left-side vertical pair at the box's MIN column which must SHIFT. Tested: 0/265 (caught the left pairs as stays). The discriminator is `k == rowmaxcol[r]` (box's rightmost col). Re-derived 2026-06-01.
- **Do NOT** use a color-blind global anchor (max r+c over all non-bg cells). Multi-color grids (180/265) need per-box anchors. Color-blind = 85/265 (only single-color grids pass).
- **Do NOT** drop the within-crop padding sentinel (`K==0 → 10`). Sub-16 grids (8×8 etc., 2,441/200,000 at size 8) have all-zero cells inside the 16×16 crop; without the sentinel they decode as ch0=1 (wrong, should be all-zero outside the active grid). The `−1` bg encoding in `K` (Conv weight `[-1,1..9]`) is what lets `Equal(K,0)` isolate padding from bg.
- **Do NOT** crop the input with `Slice` (creates a counted [1,10,16,16] F32 = 10,240) or pre-cast input to F16/U8 ([1,10,30,30] = 18,000/9,000). Reductions/Conv off the FREE `input` tensor + separable delta-Conv crop is the cheap path.
